source.title: Eliciting the Translation Ability of Large Language Models via Multilingual Finetuning with Translation Instructions
source.authors: Jia-Huan Li; Hao Zhou; Shujian Huang; Shanbo Cheng; Jia-Jun Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a scaling-like trend extends to multilingual translation instruction fine-tuning, using translation performance rather than pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: Figure 4 and its accompanying text report translation-performance trends as model parameter count and training examples vary. Other reported comparisons, such as mFTI versus ICL, do not test the scaling relation and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 4 and Section 3.3 report BLEU of fine-tuned XGLM (564M to 7.5B) as model size and fine-tuning examples per pair (1k to 32k) vary. The authors call the trend a log-linear scaling law. This is a result on downstream-task scaling (V6) in a new setting. No loss is measured, so V1 to V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record covers only the scaling sub-result, which it paraphrases correctly. The paper's main conclusions are different. Fine-tuning with translation instructions on 1k sentences per pair beats 8-shot in-context learning by about 3 BLEU. It generalises to language pairs unseen during fine-tuning. More language pairs and monolingual data reduce instruction-following errors, and pivot data improves direct alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales multilingual translation-instruction fine-tuning and evaluates translation performance, rather than fitting held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling sweep varies model parameter count and training-example count; no sensitivity to fitting choices is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: BLEU on all partitions generally rises as the number of fine-tuning language pairs grows from 16 to about 150 (Figure 5). Instruction-following errors fall at the same time (Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream translation performance improves with the number of fine-tuning tasks (language pairs).

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The scaling evidence is reported as a plotted trend without numerical curve values or uncertainty estimates. It concerns one fine-tuning translation setting and does not establish the claim about held-out pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocation.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Figure 4's individual plotted points are not numerically extractable from the text; the two rows record the aggregate trends stated by the authors.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small-run fits to larger runs.
No shape or architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No loss curves under fine-tuning or in other modalities; only BLEU is reported, which cannot show a power law in loss.
Downstream performance versus pretraining loss is not studied. No quantitative fit or predictive test is given, and only one task (translation) and one model family are covered.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling evidence is a single sentence plus Figure 4, citing Kaplan et al. as consistent. No fitted law, points or uncertainty are given. The model sizes come from the XGLM family. The record's links of R1 and R2 to V5 were removed because BLEU is not loss.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is studied.
The study does not compare architecture details such as depth and width at fixed parameter count.
Tests translation-instruction fine-tuning only; it does not test other modalities, repeated data, or transfer settings.
Reports translation performance in the fine-tuning scaling sweep, but does not study other downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitted exponents or optimal splits across fitting choices, nor report curve bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: finetuned XGLM
rows.operation_detail: Varied model parameter count and evaluated translation performance.
rows.note: The authors state that translation performance follows a standard log-linear scaling law with model size. Individual plotted values are not given in the text.
rows.check: The measure is downstream BLEU, not loss, so the row bears on V6 only, not V5's power-law loss form. The state rests on the authors' statement alone: no fitted coefficients, points or uncertainty are given.

rows.subject: finetuned XGLM
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training examples per language pair and evaluated translation performance.
rows.note: The authors state that translation performance follows a standard log-linear scaling law with the number of training examples. Individual plotted values are not given in the text.
rows.check: The scaling variable is fine-tuning examples, not pretraining scale, and the measure is BLEU, not loss. V5 asks whether the same power-law form holds under fine-tuning, which a BLEU trend cannot show. The row is evidence only on V6's downstream improvement with data scale, based on the authors' qualitative statement.

relationships.condition: XGLM 564M to 7.5B with multilingual translation-instruction fine-tuning, FLORES-101 BLEU, 1k to 32k examples per pair
relationships.reason: The authors state BLEU follows a log-linear scaling law in model size (R1) and in training examples (R2). The evidence is figure-only, with no fit numbers.
relationships.display_finding: BLEU was reported to increase log-linearly with both model size and training examples, without numerical fit results.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: XGLM translation-instruction fine-tuning, across the reported parameter-count and training-example sweeps
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe log-linear scaling of translation performance with both model size and training-example count (R1, R2); this supports extension to this fine-tuning setting, not the broader set of regimes in V5.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Translation evaluation after XGLM translation-instruction fine-tuning
reader_labels.reason: Translation performance is reported to follow a log-linear trend with model size and training-example count (R1, R2).
